title: Spectral Leakage Explorer
description: When a tone does not complete a whole number of cycles in the 512-sample frame, its energy leaks into neighboring bins. Multiplying the samples by the Hann window, w[i] = 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi i / 512), tames the leakage but always spreads a peak over about three bins.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy
Signal Processing and the FFT
Spectral Leakage
Windowing
Hann Window
Magnitude Spectrum

learningObjectives: The learner will compare the spectra of 6 test tones taken with no window and with the Hann window, and choose for each the window that gives the narrower peak, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
prerequisites: frequency bin, spectral leakage, windowing, Hann window, magnitude spectrum (all defined in this chapter above the block).

controls.purpose: Explore only: pick the window; move the tone from 900 to 1,100 Hz in steps of 6.25 Hz.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does a window always make the peak narrower? When does it not?
Where does a tone have to sit for the worst leakage without a window?
Does a quieter tone leak less? Why does the percentage scale answer this?
commonMisconceptions: (1) A window always makes the peak narrower. (2) Leakage only happens to loud tones. (3) A tone exactly on a bin leaks.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six tones. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
